section.name: Alchemical Free Energy (AFE) with Force Field X (FFX)
section.p: This guide outlines how to perform alchemical free energy calculations (e.g., relative binding or solvation) in FFX using dual/quad topologies and lambda windows, and how to analyze results.

ul.li: Topologies: FFX supports alchemical selections via atom or residue masks and dual/quad-topology constructs (--ac2, --uaA, --uaB, etc.).
Lambda: Continuously or discretely switch interactions using --lambda and switching functions.
Windows: Sample a set of lambda values (e.g., 0.0 → 1.0) and post-process via Thermodynamics (BAR/MBAR/overlap diagnostics).

ol.li: Prepare and equilibrate the reference topology at λ=0 or λ=1 (see the Preparing a Structure guide).
Define alchemical masks/topologies and validate energy evaluation at select λ values.
Minimize and equilibrate briefly at each λ.
Run production MD per λ window, saving trajectories and logs.

subsection.name: Defining alchemical systems
subsection.p: Common flags on Dynamics/Minimize (see command manpages for full details):

ul.li: --unchargedAtoms <list>: designate atoms to decouple electrostatics first.
Dual/quad topology: --ac2, --uaA, --uaB (check the Dynamics command and examples).
Switching: --lambda <value> sets the current λ; --switchingFunction {SOFTCORE|LINEAR|...} chooses the schedule.

subsection.name: Windowed MD automation
subsection.p: Create a simple bash loop or workflow manager to iterate λ windows (e.g., 0.0, 0.05, 0.1, …, 1.0). Example snippet:
subsection.source: for L in 0.00 0.05 0.10 0.20 0.35 0.50 0.65 0.80 0.90 0.95 1.00; do mkdir -p lambda_${L} cd lambda_${L} cp ../complex_equilibrated.pdb . ffxc Minimize --lambda ${L} --iterations 2000 complex_equilibrated.pdb ffxc Dynamics \ --molecularDynamicsEngine OpenMM \ --integrator Verlet \ --thermostat Bussi \ --temperature 298.15 \ --dt 1.0 \ --numberOfSteps 2000000 \ --report 1.0 --write 10.0 --checkpoint 10.0 \ --lambda ${L} \ --fileFormat XYZ \ complex_equilibrated.pdb cd .. done
subsection.p: Tune the λ schedule to ensure good overlap between adjacent windows.

subsection.name: Analysis with Thermodynamics
subsection.p: Use the Thermodynamics command to compute free energies from per-window outputs. See the Thermodynamics command.

ul.li: Ensure consistent thermostat/barostat settings across windows.
Keep trajectory/reporting/checkpoint frequencies identical for clean analysis.
Consider separate decoupling of electrostatics and van der Waals to improve convergence (use --unchargedAtoms first, then vdw scaling).
Validate end states (λ=0 and λ=1) energies and structures.
Check overlap matrices/diagnostics from Thermodynamics to refine the λ schedule.
Run multiple replicas with different random seeds to estimate uncertainty.
